But I’m happy to recommend some things that seem particularly well-suited for kids and that I think are really helpful.  The first is Scratch.  Scratch is a syntax-highlighted, block-based programming language that you can use to write code that triggers events and runs animations.  It’s very easy to get started with, and it has a lot of tutorial videos that can be found in the help menu.  The downside is that it has a very simple syntax, but for many people that’s enough to be fun.  I also recommend the Kids Coding book by Jon Udall.  It’s not the best book for starting out with Scratch, but for many kids it’s really the best book they’ll read about coding.  It’s also available as an app, so it’s really portable.  You can go through it chapter by chapter, but I think it’s best for people to just jump in and work through the exercises.  The second thing I’d recommend is Code.org’s Create with Code.  It’s a site that teaches people to code using various block languages.  It’s a lot of fun and has lots of lessons and tutorials for people of all ages, but to me it’s really helpful to have the Scratch app.  Code.org provides a lot of free lessons and projects on the Create with Code site, but for some reason they don’t have any Scratch lessons, which is a pity, because Scratch is really a great tool for starting out.  I think for kids it’s really helpful to have Scratch in the back of their mind, to just keep a little copy of the official Scratch code in a folder on their computer, just so they can play around with it and experiment.  It can be really fun to do that, and for me it’s really helpful to remind me that I’m actually doing something really useful!  Coding is really useful, it really is, it does make our lives so much easier to have machines that can do all the simple tasks that we used to do ourselves, but to me it’s really fun to do things myself, and to have the ability to write code is an important tool in that.  So for kids it’s really important that they feel like they can have fun with it.  I’m very supportive of Scratch, and I think their lessons use Scratch, and their tutorials explain how to use Scratch, which is really helpful, but I think also it helps a lot if kids just have Scratch on their computers and can play with it.  In fact one of the best things that Code.org does is provide Scratch projects, which are blocks that can be dragged and dropped in a web browser to create things.  It really helps kids start out making something, and then they can see what it looks like when they drag it into a browser.  That’s really helpful for them to see that what they’ve written is actually going to do something.  One last thing is that I think it’s really helpful for kids to have their own computer, or at least a computer that has free internet, so they can play with Scratch and other coding games.  My kids have used our library computers, but it can be really hard for kids to work at home, so even if you don’t have a library computer it might be worth checking if your kids can use the internet at home.  I’d also recommend that they get a USB dongle that allows them to use a computer with their phones and tablets.  You can get ones that support Android, iOS and Windows, so if you don’t have one of those you could still use it in most cases.  The USB dongle allows you to write code in Scratch, and you can just drag it onto your phone or tablet, so it won’t stop you from playing with Scratch.  I also recommend that they get a Scratch device pack.  You can buy these at many craft stores, you can even get them at some electronics stores.  They look kind of like little toy robots, and they work really well for making Scratch projects.  My husband bought one of these and some Scratch blocks for our kids, and I think it was really helpful to see what they looked like.
